- KNOWN contextual evidence: a health-protection pilot was associated with lower medical spending, and a flood cash trial found mixed effects across outcomes and timing. Neither establishes a general heat effect. (Sources: Hasan et al., 2024: The effectiveness of a government-sponsored health protection scheme in reducing financial risks for the below-poverty-line population in Bangladesh https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/30215/1/FullText.pdf; Christian et al., 2025: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal https://bfi.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/BFI_WP_2025-140.pdf)

- Not verified: universal heat income replacement, a public heat-specific medical claims pathway, portable informal-worker protection, and a complete last-mile evidence base. No result is interpreted as proof that households are unprotected. (Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf; Hasan et al., 2024: The effectiveness of a government-sponsored health protection scheme in reducing financial risks for the below-poverty-line population in Bangladesh https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/30215/1/FullText.pdf; International Labour Organization: Implementation of a pilot Employment Injury Scheme (EIS) in Bangladesh https://www.ilo.org/projects-and-partnerships/projects/implementation-pilot-employment-injury-scheme-eis-bangladesh)

#### Schemes in Bangladesh

- Family Card Programme (Cash, national). Run by: Department of Social Services. Who is eligible: Selected low-income households. What it gives: Tk. 2,500 monthly. How it is delivered: Government-to-person payment. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Vulnerable Women Benefit (Food, national). Run by: Department of Women Affairs. Who is eligible: Not confirmed in the source we checked; see the source. What it gives: 30 kg rice monthly. How it is delivered: Food distribution. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Employment Generation Programme for the Poorest (Public works, national). Run by: Department of Disaster Management. Who is eligible: Selected unemployed workers in poverty. What it gives: Tk. 500 daily worker rate. How it is delivered: Public works; Job Card. Documents: Job Card is described; current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Published weekly payment cycle; actual delay unknown. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: paid work can cushion income, while outdoor work also creates heat exposure. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Food Friendly Programme (Food, national). Run by: Directorate General of Food. Who is eligible: Registered rural households in poverty. What it gives: 30 kg rice monthly for six months at Tk. 15/kg. How it is delivered: Union-level dealers. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Vulnerable Group Feeding (Food, national). Run by: Department of Disaster Management. Who is eligible: Selected households facing poverty or shocks. What it gives: Rice assistance; allocation depends on distribution round. How it is delivered: Local food distribution. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: resources could help meet hot-season household costs; heat outcomes were not evaluated. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Rural Social Services Programme (Credit, national). Run by: Department of Social Services. Who is eligible: Low-income rural households, including landless households. What it gives: Published revolving loan range: Tk. 5,000-50,000 per family; local offer not verified. How it is delivered: Public rural credit programme. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: credit may support livelihood recovery; repayment also affects household budgets. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Financial Assistance for Patients Suffering from Cancer, Kidney Disease, Liver Cirrhosis, Stroke Paralysis, Congenital Heart Disease and Thalassaemia (Health care, national). Run by: Department of Social Services. Who is eligible: Specified illnesses and financial conditions. What it gives: Up to Tk. 100,000 one-time assistance. How it is delivered: Medical-assistance process. Documents: Medical certification; full current checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: No general heat-illness entitlement was verified in this disease-specific scheme. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf

- Employment Injury Scheme pilot (Insurance, national). Run by: Ministry of Labour and Employment / Central Fund. Who is eligible: Covered ready-made garment workers. What it gives: Employment-injury support; individual formula not verified. How it is delivered: Central Fund pilot arrangements. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Heat-related occupational claims were not verified; informal and construction coverage cannot be assumed. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: International Labour Organization: Implementation of a pilot Employment Injury Scheme (EIS) in Bangladesh https://www.ilo.org/projects-and-partnerships/projects/implementation-pilot-employment-injury-scheme-eis-bangladesh

- Shasthyo Suroksha Karmasuchi (Health care, national). Run by: Health Economics Unit, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Who is eligible: Below-poverty-line pilot population in the evaluated locations. What it gives: Not confirmed in the source we checked; see the source. How it is delivered: Pilot contracted care in the historical evaluation. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: hospital-cost protection could help; heat-specific claims were not studied. Status: Status unclear, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Not yet confirmed. Sources: Hasan et al., 2024: The effectiveness of a government-sponsored health protection scheme in reducing financial risks for the below-poverty-line population in Bangladesh https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/30215/1/FullText.pdf

#### Steps of access in Bangladesh (findings come from different studies of different people; they are not one funnel)

- Aware: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?

- Eligible: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?

- Documented: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?

- Applied: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?

- Enrolled: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?

- Received: Implementers report 301 recipients received a BDT 2,400 top-up in August 2025. (Simulation participants in Ward 4, Rajshahi; limit: Selected simulation participants; no population access denominator or independent outcome evaluation.; sources: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre and implementing partners, 2026: When social protection anticipates risk: Lessons from a shock responsive social protection simulation in Rajshahi city, Bangladesh https://www.anticipation-hub.org/Documents/Reports/0_RCCC_SRSP_simulation_Rajshahi_Advocacy_brief_V3.pdf)
- Received: Implementer update: 1,290 households had received multipurpose cash by 27 April 2024. (Selected Dhaka households; limit: The 4,000-household figure is a target, not the receipt count in this update.; sources: Bangladesh Red Crescent Society, 2024: Nationwide Heatwave Early Actions/Response: Operations Update-01; 27 April, 2024 https://bdrcs.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Heatwave-Early-Actions-2024-_27.4.24-_Operation-Update-01.pdf)

- Adequate: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: When heat arrives, how much of a household's lost earnings and care costs does an allowance or top-up cover, and does it arrive before the hottest days?

- On time: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: When heat arrives, how much of a household's lost earnings and care costs does an allowance or top-up cover, and does it arrive before the hottest days?

#### Where no public system responds in Bangladesh (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Informal and outdoor workers' heat-related lost earnings: no automatic nationwide public wage-replacement entitlement was verified in the schemes read; targeted allowances and works programmes cover selected groups. (Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf; International Labour Organization: Implementation of a pilot Employment Injury Scheme (EIS) in Bangladesh https://www.ilo.org/projects-and-partnerships/projects/implementation-pilot-employment-injury-scheme-eis-bangladesh)

- General heat illness and outpatient costs: the disease-specific assistance list does not establish general heat coverage; the SSK evaluation does not report heat claims. (Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf; Hasan et al., 2024: The effectiveness of a government-sponsored health protection scheme in reducing financial risks for the below-poverty-line population in Bangladesh https://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/30215/1/FullText.pdf)

- Crop loss and agricultural debt: public rural credit was identified, but no verified heat-triggered payout or debt pause was found in the sources read. This is an evidence gap, not a claim that no agricultural programme exists. (Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf)

- Seasonal migration: nationwide portability of eligibility, applications and collection was not verified; a digital transfer alone does not establish portability. (Sources: Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, 2026: Social Security Budget Report FY2026-27 https://objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com/n/axvjbnqprylg/b/V2Ministry/o/office-mof/2026/5/4d4de077-26a7-4f8f-aad1-7b3f48043897.pdf)

- Heat debt, asset sales and mortality: no evaluated public heat transfer effect was found in this bounded search. Flood trial findings do not fill that gap. (Sources: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre and implementing partners, 2026: When social protection anticipates risk: Lessons from a shock responsive social protection simulation in Rajshahi city, Bangladesh https://www.anticipation-hub.org/Documents/Reports/0_RCCC_SRSP_simulation_Rajshahi_Advocacy_brief_V3.pdf; Bangladesh Red Crescent Society, 2024: Nationwide Heatwave Early Actions/Response: Operations Update-01; 27 April, 2024 https://bdrcs.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Heatwave-Early-Actions-2024-_27.4.24-_Operation-Update-01.pdf; Christian et al., 2025: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal https://bfi.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/BFI_WP_2025-140.pdf)

#### Open questions for Bangladesh (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- Does an allowance top-up before a heatwave reduce lost work and medical spending? What is known: A Rajshahi delivery simulation was reported. [B5] A study that could answer it: Randomised phased invitation or top-up timing across comparable neighbourhood clusters, with aggregate income, medical-spending and timing outcomes. (Illustrative design: 40-60 clusters; final size from power calculations.)

- At which access step do heat-exposed urban households stop receiving support? What is known: HIES measures past receipt but not a linked eligibility-to-receipt ladder. [B3] A study that could answer it: A repeated representative household survey linked only to consented, de-identified process totals; publish aggregate transitions and reasons. (Illustrative design: 1,500-2,000 households across several cities.)

- How often does public support meet the costs of medically diagnosed heat illness? What is known: A historical SSK financial-risk evaluation exists; heat-specific claims were not reported. [B7] A study that could answer it: Prospective facility-cost study comparing public benefits, out-of-pocket costs, referral and foregone care across one hot season. (Illustrative design: 10-15 facilities; power and case-volume check first.)

- Does assisted application improve timely receipt among migrants and women outdoor workers? What is known: Delivery organisations describe support, but no comparable independent local effect was read. [B6, B12, B13] A study that could answer it: Randomise outreach timing among consenting community clusters and track aggregate application, receipt, cost and delay. (Illustrative design: 30-50 clusters over one application cycle.)

- [Unmeasured: Adequate, On time] When heat arrives, how much of a household's lost earnings and care costs does an allowance or top-up cover, and does it arrive before the hottest days? What is known: Implementer reports count households that received cash in Rajshahi and Dhaka. None of the sources checked measures how far the money went, or when it arrived compared with the heat. A study that could answer it: Follow recipient households through one hot season, recording lost work days, care costs and payment dates against heat-alert dates. (Illustrative: about 300 households in two cities over one hot season)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible, Documented, Applied, Enrolled] How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled? What is known: None of the sources checked measures these steps for the schemes on this page in Bangladesh. A study that could answer it: A household survey in hot wards that asks the same people about each step, for the same schemes. (Illustrative: about 1,000 households in four wards)

### India (research as of 5 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- Official announcements describe rural-employment changes from July 2026 and pension changes approved in October. Pension implementation and current disaster-relief details remain partly unverified. (Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Historic Commencement of Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act Across Rural India from July 1st 2026 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2259703&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable; Ministry of Home Affairs: Disaster Management Division https://www.mha.gov.in/index.php/disaster-management-division)

- Openly licensed weather data can support state exposure indicators. Public reports provide other indicators, but reuse licences and shared place codes are not consistently established. (Sources: Copernicus Climate Change Service / ECMWF, 2018: ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels?tab=overview; Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars; India Meteorological Department: Yearly Gridded Maximum Temperature (1.0 x 1.0) data Binary File https://imdpune.gov.in/cmpg/Griddata/Max_1_Bin.html; International Institute for Population Sciences and ICF, 2022: National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 2019-21: India https://assets.exemplars.health/fd9a20fb-4386-00b3-39a1-1737868b44b7/d4b76902-0381-4d15-9661-9b2e06b58682/10%20National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%205%2020192021.pdf; geoBoundaries: Archival & Programmatic Access https://www.geoboundaries.org/api.html)

#### Schemes in India

- Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (Public works, national). Run by: Ministry of Rural Development and state governments. Who is eligible: Rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. What it gives: 125 days of wage employment per financial year; wage rates vary. How it is delivered: Work on demand; wages through bank or post-office accounts. Documents: Existing job cards remain valid; the complete new application checklist was not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Published rule: weekly payment or within fifteen days of muster-roll closure; actual receipt times not verified. Why it matters in heat: Could replace some lost rural earnings, depending on work availability, safe conditions and payment timing. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Historic Commencement of Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act Across Rural India from July 1st 2026 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2259703&lang=1&reg=1

- Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: People in below-poverty-line households aged 60 or above under continuing central rules. What it gives: Central assistance: Rs.200 monthly at ages 60-79; Rs.500 at 80 or above. State additions vary. How it is delivered: State pension systems. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Regular income could help meet seasonal household costs. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Widows in below-poverty-line households aged 40 or above under continuing central rules. What it gives: Central assistance: Rs.300 monthly at ages 40-79; Rs.500 at 80 or above. State additions vary. How it is delivered: State pension systems. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Regular income could cushion seasonal earnings pressure. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: October approval expands eligibility to 40% benchmark disability and removes the minimum age; operational commencement not verified. What it gives: Approved central rates: Rs.375 monthly at ages 0-79 and Rs.625 at 80 or above. How it is delivered: State pension systems; transition guidelines pending in the announcement. Documents: Revised operational checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual timing unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could support recurring costs for households including people with disabilities. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana (Cash, national). Run by: Department of Rural Development and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Surviving household head of a below-poverty-line family after the death of its primary breadwinner aged 18-59. What it gives: Rs.20,000 under continuing central rules. How it is delivered: State-administered, demand-based assistance. Documents: State checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could assist an eligible family following a breadwinner's death; heat-specific receipt not verified. Status: Changed recently, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1; Government of India, 2026: Cabinet approves continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-continuation-of-the-national-social-assistance-programme-for-five-years-from-2026-27-to-2030-31/?comment=disable

- National Food Security Act foodgrain entitlement under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (Food, national). Run by: Department of Food and Public Distribution and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household beneficiaries identified by states/UTs; Maharashtra rules checked. What it gives: 35 kg per Antyodaya household monthly; 5 kg per Priority Household person monthly. Free foodgrains continue through 31 December 2028. How it is delivered: Public Distribution System. Documents: State ration-card enrolment requirements vary; complete current checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly entitlement; household receipt dates unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could preserve food consumption when earnings fall; no automatic heat-related increase verified. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Maharashtra Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Department: National Food Security Act, 2013 https://s3e21e4e58ad9ab56e8a4634046da90113.s3waas.gov.in/national-food-security-act-2013/; Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars

- Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (Pension, national). Run by: Ministry of Labour and Employment. Who is eligible: Eligible unorganised workers entering at ages 18-40, subject to income and other pension or insurance exclusions. What it gives: Rs.3,000 monthly from age 60; contributory rather than immediate income support. How it is delivered: Common Service Centres or Maandhan portal; contributions through auto-debit. Documents: Aadhaar, savings or Jan-Dhan account details with IFSC, and mobile number. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Pension starts at age 60; not a current-season payment for new entrants. Why it matters in heat: Relevant to future old-age income rather than current heat-related earnings losses. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment: Schemes https://eshram.gov.in/Schemes; Ministry of Labour and Employment, 2025: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/2e7e01b90e6358cb82f396615fc87a94.pdf

- Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (Insurance, national). Run by: Government-supported life insurance through participating banks and insurers. Who is eligible: Eligible account holders entering at ages 18-50 with consent for premium auto-debit. What it gives: Rs.2 lakh on death from any cause; annual premium Rs.436. How it is delivered: Bank-linked insurance claim. Documents: Account and enrolment consent; complete claim checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual claim-to-payment time unknown. Why it matters in heat: Death cover could help eligible surviving households; not earnings replacement during non-fatal illness. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment: Schemes https://eshram.gov.in/Schemes

- National Health Mission Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Service Initiatives (Health care, national). Run by: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and states/UTs. Who is eligible: Patients using participating public health facilities. What it gives: Specified essential medicines and diagnostic services free of cost; no household cash amount. How it is delivered: Public facilities, with packages differing by facility level. Documents: No uniform household application checklist verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Care-linked provision; actual availability and waiting time unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could reduce treatment costs, including outside hospital insurance; heat-specific availability not measured in the source. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2026: Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2292343&lang=2&reg=48

- Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Insurance, national). Run by: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, participating states and insurers. Who is eligible: Eligible farmers with insured crops in notified areas, including tenants and sharecroppers meeting state documentation conditions. What it gives: Claims depend on insured loss and sum insured. Maximum farmer premiums: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi foodgrain/oilseed crops, 5% commercial/horticultural crops. How it is delivered: Implementing insurers and enrolment channels. Documents: Insurable interest and state-defined land, tenure or sowing evidence; application and premium within deadlines. Does not follow people who move. Can respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual claim timing not verified. Why it matters in heat: Some heat-related crop losses could enter insured yield loss; universal farm-level heat trigger not verified. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Press Information Bureau, 2026: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2304549&lang=1&reg=48

- Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (Credit, national). Run by: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through lending institutions. Who is eligible: Eligible short-term agricultural borrowers, including specified allied activities. What it gives: 2026-27 budget note: loans up to ₹3 lakh at 7% yearly, with an additional 3% benefit for prompt repayment. How it is delivered: Concessional agricultural lending. Documents: Lender-specific checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: Sanction and disbursement times unknown. Why it matters in heat: Could provide seasonal liquidity; repayable borrowing, not a heat-loss grant. Status: Current, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Government of India, 2026: Notes on Demands for Grants, 2026-2027 https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe1.pdf

- Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board benefits (Workers' welfare fund, state). Run by: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. Who is eligible: Registered workers meeting Board age, work-history and contribution conditions. What it gives: Medical and other assistance. Medical payment wording is difficult to interpret, so no reliable payable amount is reproduced. How it is delivered: Applications through area Labour Inspector. Documents: Registration: photograph, age proof, employer certificate of 90 days' construction work. Medical claims list hospital records and subscription evidence. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Unknown. Why it matters in heat: Medical assistance could help qualifying workers; heat-specific approvals and payments not verified. Status: Status unclear, as of 5 November 2026. Evidence: Not yet confirmed. Sources: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Frequently Asked Questions https://megbocwwb.gov.in/faqs; Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Schemes https://megbocwwb.gov.in/schemes

#### Steps of access in India (findings come from different studies of different people; they are not one funnel)

- Aware: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?

- Eligible: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?

- Documented: India, 31 October 2025: 68,14,95,972 beneficiaries completed e-KYC, stated as 85.6%. (Existing NFSA beneficiaries; limit: e-KYC is neither receipt nor every documentation requirement.; sources: Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars)

- Applied: December 2025 parliamentary reply: the Department does not maintain the pendency list. (Households awaiting a card or addition of members; limit: Describes the central record; state records may exist.; sources: Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2025: E-KYC COMPLIANT RATION CARDS https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1793_fjXAYl.pdf?source=pqars)

- Enrolled: India, NFHS-5, 2019-21: 41.0% had any usual member covered by a health insurance or financing scheme. (Households across health insurance and financing schemes; limit: Self-reported household coverage; not a PM-JAY enrolment rate or evidence of care received.; sources: International Institute for Population Sciences and ICF, 2022: National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 2019-21: India https://assets.exemplars.health/fd9a20fb-4386-00b3-39a1-1737868b44b7/d4b76902-0381-4d15-9661-9b2e06b58682/10%20National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%205%2020192021.pdf)

- Received: India, as of 30 June 2026: 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions authorised. (Beneficiaries accessing care outside their home state; limit: Authorisations are a proxy, not unique people or verified completed care; no heat-specific costs measured.; sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2026: Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY) https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290627&lang=1&reg=22)
- Received: India, 1 April to 2 December 2025: women accounted for 56.73% of person-days. (Women in historical MGNREGA; limit: Work participation proxy, not wage receipt or eligible-women coverage.; sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1)

- Adequate: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs?

- On time: India, 1 April to 2 December 2025: 95.31% of fund transfer orders generated within 8 days. (Historical MGNREGA workers; limit: Administrative stage, not bank receipt; predates July 2026 transition.; sources: Ministry of Rural Development, 2026: Department of Rural Development: Year Ender 2025 https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1)

#### Delivery routes and organisations in India (unranked)

- Common Service Centres (government). Provide assisted registration, authentication and applications for specified schemes. Where: India. What it says about itself: No consistently dated reach figure retained.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Where: India; precise current footprint not verified.. What it says about itself: No independently checked membership or insurance reach retained.. What independent studies found: External page specifies a planned encouragement study; no results.. Sources: Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab, 2025: Insuring Against Extreme Heat: A Randomised Evaluation https://www.povertyactionlab.org/initiative-project/insuring-against-extreme-heat-randomised-evaluation

- India Post Payments Bank (financial). Provides an account route for eligible transfers, with Aadhaar seeding through app or post office. Where: India. What it says about itself: No dated reach retained.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: India Post Payments Bank: Direct Benefit Transfers https://ippbonline.bank.in/web/ippb/direct-benefit-transfers

- National Legal Services Authority and local legal services institutions (government). Provide eligible legal assistance; paralegal volunteers can help with oral applications and government schemes. Where: India through state, district and local institutions.. What it says about itself: No dated scheme-access reach retained.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: National Legal Services Authority: Legal Aid https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/

- Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitras (government). Help with PM-JAY verification, cashless admissions and hospital support. Where: Participating hospitals in India.. What it says about itself: Programme admissions are not attributable assistance effects.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2026: Update on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna (AB PM-JAY) https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290627&lang=1&reg=22

- e-Shram (digital platform). Registers unorganised workers and connects specified scheme information; registration is not a payment. Where: India. What it says about itself: No dated registration total retained.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment: FAQs https://eshram.gov.in/faqs

#### Where no public system responds in India (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Income lost while resting: no national automatic heat-triggered informal-worker wage replacement verified. Delhi evidence records earnings losses. (Sources: Das and Somanathan, 2024: Heat causes large earnings losses for informal-sector workers in India https://heathealth.info/wp-content/uploads/Das_2024_Environ._Res._Lett._19_124019.pdf)

- Farm losses outside insurance conditions: PMFBY depends on notification, enrolment and covered risks. (Sources: Press Information Bureau, 2026: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2304549&lang=1&reg=48)

- Current shocks for new pension entrants: PM-SYM pays from age 60. (Sources: Ministry of Labour and Employment, 2025: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) https://www.labour.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/2e7e01b90e6358cb82f396615fc87a94.pdf)

- Debt and asset sales: no verified evaluation links public-system receipt to reductions in these heat outcomes.

- Anticipatory payments: no current public heat-forecast-triggered cash entitlement with verified rules and receipt established.

- Construction workers outside registration: checked Meghalaya benefits depend on the Board's qualifying route. (Sources: Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Frequently Asked Questions https://megbocwwb.gov.in/faqs; Meghalaya Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board: Schemes https://megbocwwb.gov.in/schemes)

#### Open questions for India (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- At which access step do heat-exposed informal-worker households lose the most potential support? What is known: Separate administrative stocks and a small commissioned facilitation assessment; no complete representative ladder. A study that could answer it: Voluntary repeated survey before, during and after a hot season, publishing only aggregate group and step results. (About 1,500 households across six districts; final size depends on detectable differences.)

- Does receiving an existing transfer before peak heat improve coping compared with later receipt? What is known: Entitlements and heat earnings-loss evidence; little verified payment-timing evidence. A study that could answer it: Evaluate an authorised timing change with aggregate earnings, care costs and borrowing outcomes. (About 2,000 households across 40-60 clusters, subject to power analysis.)

- How much of household heat-illness cost is met through PM-JAY and free public care? What is known: Hospital-cover rules and service policies; no verified heat-specific cost pathway. A study that could answer it: Consent-based care-cost study across public and empanelled facilities, publishing aggregate results. (About 600 episodes across 12 facilities in one season.)

- Does assisted scheme navigation improve timely receipt during a hot season? What is known: Delivery models and commissioned assessment; no verified heat-specific causal estimate. A study that could answer it: Phased rollout of additional support against existing services, measuring receipt and timing; providers on equal terms. (About 60 communities and 1,800 households; subject to power analysis.)

- Can public works cushion heat income loss while reducing exposure? What is known: Historical learning protection evidence; no verified 2026-framework heat evaluation. A study that could answer it: Evaluate adjusted hours, rest and water provision alongside work access and wage arrival. (About 50 worksites across four districts in one hot season.)

- [Unmeasured: Adequate] Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs? What is known: Documents, applications, enrolment, receipt and payment timing are measured for some schemes, such as fund transfer orders for rural work. No source checked measures whether support is adequate in a hot season. A study that could answer it: Compare the support received with heat-season losses in the same households, in a hot month and a cooler one. (Illustrative: about 600 households in three districts)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible] How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify? What is known: Later steps are measured for some schemes; awareness and eligibility are not, in the sources checked. A study that could answer it: Pair a short awareness survey with an eligibility screen for the same workers, at worksites and markets. (Illustrative: about 800 workers in two cities)

### Indonesia (research as of 6 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- KNOWN heat evidence: insured primary-care visits increased on hotter days, including diabetes and cardiovascular visits. That study does not estimate how much insurance reduced household heat losses. (Sources: Fritz, 2022: Temperature and non-communicable diseases: Evidence from Indonesia's primary health care system https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hec.4590)

- KNOWN contextual evidence: PKH improved some child outcomes but did not increase several household economic outcomes in its historic evaluation. No heat-specific PKH causal effect was verified. (Sources: J-PAL: The Medium-Term Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Health and Education in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/medium-term-impact-conditional-cash-transfers-health-and-education-indonesia; Cahyadi et al., 2020: Cumulative Impacts of Conditional Cash Transfer Programs: Experimental Evidence from Indonesia https://swlb1.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pol.20190245)

- INFERRED map design: open climate and modelled population grids can be aggregated to a documented older province geography. Public source metadata reveals a boundary-vintage issue, so current province coverage tables are not silently joined. [Ie, Iw, Ib]

#### Schemes in Indonesia

- Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja: Bukan Penerima Upah (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Registered and contributing non-wage workers. What it gives: Medically necessary work-injury care and temporary incapacity compensation. How it is delivered: BPJS claim route; registration assistance listed in section E. Documents: NIK or KTP and email for registration; claim documents need a separate check. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Work attribution and acceptance of heat-related claims were not verified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Kematian: Bukan Penerima Upah (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Active contributors and qualifying survivors under programme conditions. What it gives: Death grant Rp20.000.000, periodic grant Rp12.000.000 and funeral Rp10.000.000. How it is delivered: Survivor claim through BPJS. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: survivor support could cushion a death-related shock; work and non-work pathways differ. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Hari Tua: Bukan Penerima Upah (Pension, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Contributors meeting withdrawal conditions. What it gives: Accumulated contributions plus investment returns; no fixed universal pension. How it is delivered: BPJS withdrawal process. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: Savings are distinct from an immediate heat-triggered grant. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html

- Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja and Jaminan Kematian: Jasa Konstruksi (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Who is eligible: Covered construction-project workers. What it gives: JKK treatment and temporary incapacity pay: 100% for the first and second six-month periods, then 50%. How it is delivered: Project and BPJS arrangements. Documents: Current application checklist not verified. Not known whether it follows people who move. Not known whether it responds to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: A relevant outdoor-worker route, with heat-specific paid-claim evidence unverified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Jaminan Keselamatan Kerja untuk Jasa Konstruksi (Jakon) https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jasa-konstruksi.html

- Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan (Insurance, national). Run by: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan / Ministry of Manpower. Who is eligible: Qualifying wage workers with employment termination and contribution history. What it gives: 60% of reported wage for up to six months; wage ceiling Rp. 5.000.000,00. How it is delivered: Monthly claims and labour-market services. Documents: Termination evidence and active job-search commitment; other conditions apply. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Monthly benefit; actual processing distribution unknown. Why it matters in heat: Termination protection does not automatically replace income for a temporary hot day. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Cek Informasi Detail Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jaminan-kehilangan-pekerjaan.html

- Bantuan Subsidi Upah 2026 (Cash, national). Run by: Ministry of Manpower. Who is eligible: Qualifying citizens active as wage-earner BPJS members through August 2026; wage and other tests apply. What it gives: Not confirmed in the source we checked; see the source. How it is delivered: BPJS-sourced selection; current page awaits further recipient-check details. Documents: NIK and administrative employment/wage records; applicant process not fully announced. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: General purchasing-power support; no heat forecast trigger verified. Status: Changed recently, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Ministry of Manpower, 2026: Bantuan Subsidi Upah 2026 https://bsu.kemnaker.go.id/

- Kredit Usaha Rakyat: BRI offer (Credit, national). Run by: Government credit programme / Bank Rakyat Indonesia. Who is eligible: Productive viable enterprises meeting lender tests. What it gives: Super-micro up to Rp10 million at 3%; micro above Rp10 million to Rp100 million, starting at 6% yearly. How it is delivered: Participating lender; BRI terms checked. Documents: BRI 2026 offer lists NIB and NPWP; additional lender documents apply. Not known whether it follows people who move. Can partly respond to a shock. Payment timing: Actual payment time not measured in the sources read. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: working capital can help livelihoods, while the full loan remains repayable. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Bank Rakyat Indonesia, 2026: Kredit Usaha Rakyat (KUR) https://bri.co.id/web/guest/promo-detail/900

#### Steps of access in Indonesia (findings come from different studies of different people; they are not one funnel)

- Aware: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?

- Eligible: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?

- Documented: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?

- Applied: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?

- Enrolled: Evaluation of 5,996 households: registration assistance increased enrolment by 3.5 percentage points. (Non-poor informal-worker households in Bandung and Medan; limit: Historical randomised offer, not current national access; page narrative describes 2015-2018.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)
- Enrolled: Full subsidy increased enrolment by 18.6 percentage points from a comparison mean of 7.8 percent. (Same historical evaluation population; limit: Subsidy experiment; not a 2026 policy coverage estimate.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)
- Enrolled: Additional information had no measured effect on enrolment. (Same historical evaluation population; limit: Specific information treatments and historical urban sample; not proof that all awareness work has no effect.; sources: J-PAL: Enrolling Informal Sector Workers in National Health Insurance in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/enrolling-informal-sector-workers-national-health-insurance-indonesia)

- Received: Government report, 7 August 2026: more than 7 million families had been paid in quarter III. (Programme families; limit: Interim national administrative report; no eligible-family denominator or heat subgroup.; sources: Ministry of State Secretariat, 2026: Pastikan Tepat Sasaran, Pemerintah Salurkan Bansos kepada Lebih dari 18 Juta KPM https://www.setneg.go.id/baca/index/pastikan_tepat_sasaran_pemerintah_salurkan_bansos_kepada_lebih_dari_18_juta_kpm)
- Received: Government report, 7 August 2026: more than 12 million families had been paid in quarter III. (Programme families; limit: Not a completed-quarter count; cannot sum overlapping schemes.; sources: Ministry of State Secretariat, 2026: Pastikan Tepat Sasaran, Pemerintah Salurkan Bansos kepada Lebih dari 18 Juta KPM https://www.setneg.go.id/baca/index/pastikan_tepat_sasaran_pemerintah_salurkan_bansos_kepada_lebih_dari_18_juta_kpm)

- Adequate: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work?

- On time: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work?

#### Delivery routes and organisations in Indonesia (unranked)

- PKH social facilitators (government). Current government reporting identifies facilitators supporting programme households. Where: Indonesia. What it says about itself: No separate measured heat-season application-success count.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Ministry of State Secretariat, 2026: Pastikan Tepat Sasaran, Pemerintah Salurkan Bansos kepada Lebih dari 18 Juta KPM https://www.setneg.go.id/baca/index/pastikan_tepat_sasaran_pemerintah_salurkan_bansos_kepada_lebih_dari_18_juta_kpm

- BRILink and BNI46 agent routes (financial). BPJS lists these as enrolment and contribution channels. Where: Indonesia. What it says about itself: No independently evaluated heat outcome verified.. #### Where no public system responds in Indonesia (gaps in the checked scheme set, not proof that nothing exists)

- Informal heat work stoppages: JKK concerns qualifying work injury and JKP concerns qualifying termination; neither opened rule establishes general pay for every lost hot day. (Sources: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Manfaat Bukan Penerima Upah https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/Bukan-Penerima-Upah.html; BPJS Ketenagakerjaan: Cek Informasi Detail Jaminan Kehilangan Pekerjaan https://www.bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id/jaminan-kehilangan-pekerjaan.html)

- Heat debt, asset sales and mortality: no evaluated public heat-transfer effect was opened. Non-heat PKH null findings are not heat null findings. (Sources: J-PAL: The Medium-Term Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Health and Education in Indonesia https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/medium-term-impact-conditional-cash-transfers-health-and-education-indonesia; Cahyadi et al., 2020: Cumulative Impacts of Conditional Cash Transfer Programs: Experimental Evidence from Indonesia https://swlb1.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pol.20190245)

#### Open questions for Indonesia (study designs and sizes are our suggestions; sizes are illustrative)

- What share of diagnosed work-related heat claims reach benefit payment? What is known: JKK benefits exist; heat-specific acceptance and delay were not verified. [I5, I6] A study that could answer it: Prospective multi-site claims pathway study, publishing aggregate submitted, accepted and paid counts and time intervals. (Illustrative: several provinces over two hot seasons; sample based on case volume.)

- Does contribution support keep informal workers insured through the hot season? What is known: A registration experiment and a new contribution-saving route exist. [I16, I9] A study that could answer it: Cluster randomisation of assisted contribution-saving access, measuring active coverage, care costs and retention in aggregate. (Illustrative: 40-60 clusters; final size from power calculations.)

- Does a pre-heat top-up reduce income loss, debt and delayed care? What is known: PKH delivery and general economic evaluations exist, without a verified heat effect. [I4, I17] A study that could answer it: Pre-specified phased top-up trial using forecasts, with household outcomes reported only in aggregate. (Illustrative: two hot seasons across 40-60 clusters.)

- Which heat-related crop losses meet AUTP damage rules and receive timely support? What is known: Drought insurance terms and extension routes are published. [I11] A study that could answer it: Crop-season panel combining weather, field loss assessment and anonymised aggregate claim outcomes, without publishing farm locations. (Illustrative: 1,000-1,500 insured and comparable uninsured farm households.)

- [Unmeasured: On time, Adequate] Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work? What is known: Government reports count the families paid each quarter, without payment dates set against heat or amounts set against losses. A study that could answer it: Link payment dates with heat records and a short household survey on lost work and spending. (Illustrative: about 500 families in two provinces over one year)

- [Unmeasured: Aware, Eligible, Documented, Applied] Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it? What is known: An evaluation in Bandung and Medan measured enrolment: registration help raised it by 3.5 percentage points and full subsidy by 18.6, while information alone had no measured effect. Awareness, documents and applications were not measured as separate steps. A study that could answer it: Follow the same workers through awareness, documents and application, with and without help to register. (Illustrative: about 1,000 workers in two cities)

### Nepal (research as of 6 November 2026; sources checked 7 November 2026)

- UNCERTAIN current rule: official allowance pages and an agency budget brief differ on the general old-age threshold. The child allowance also has a budget-announced change whose receipt was not verified. (Sources: Department of National ID and Civil Registration: प्राय सोधिने प्रश्नहरु : सामाजिक सुरक्षा https://www.donidcr.gov.np/pages/mostly-asked-questions--social-security-4/; Department of National ID and Civil Registration: Social Security Allowance Rate https://donidcr.gov.np/pages/social-security-allowance-rate/; UNICEF Nepal, 2026: Nepal Federal Budget Brief: Fiscal Year 2026/27 (2083/84 B.S.) https://www.unicef.org/nepal/media/31216/file/Federal%20Budget%20Brief-2026_UNICEF_Web%20Version.pdf.pdf)

- KNOWN plan: a November 2025 urban heatwave protocol identifies cash and delivery routes. No completed causal heat-transfer outcome evaluation was verified in this search. (Sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/downloadfile/93851/sEAP2025NP02_MDRNP020)

- Evidence is thin on heat-related paid claims, informal-worker wage replacement, migrant access and household debt or asset recovery. Flood cash evidence offers a study design, rather than a demonstrated heat effect. (Sources: Social Security Fund: अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र सामाजिक सुरक्षा योजना https://www.ssf.gov.np/list/operating-schemes/informal-sector-scheme; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/downloadfile/93851/sEAP2025NP02_MDRNP020; Christian et al., 2025: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal https://bfi.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/BFI_WP_2025-140.pdf)

- Social Security Allowance: general older citizens (Pension, national). Run by: Government of Nepal / local governments. Who is eligible: Not confirmed in the source we checked; see the source. - Social Security Allowance: Dalit and specified-area older citizens (Pension, national). Run by: Government of Nepal / local governments. How it is delivered: Ward registration and bank payment. Documents: Citizenship and application; category verification applies. Partly follows people who move. Not designed to respond to a shock. Payment timing: FAQ: eligibility starts the month after verification and system entry; observed bank-payment delay unknown. Why it matters in heat: INFERRED: regular cash can support hot-season consumption; no automatic heat top-up was verified. Status: Current, as of 6 November 2026. Evidence: Confirmed in the sources. Sources: Department of National ID and Civil Registration: प्राय सोधिने प्रश्नहरु : सामाजिक सुरक्षा https://www.donidcr.gov.np/pages/mostly-asked-questions--social-security-4/; Department of National ID and Civil Registration: Social Security Allowance Rate https://donidcr.gov.np/pages/social-security-allowance-rate/

#### Steps of access in Nepal (findings come from different studies of different people; they are not one funnel)

- Aware: 2023, before informal-sector launch: 9 percent knew of SSF. (Informal workers in the urban parental-benefits survey; limit: Urban sample with a parental-benefits focus; pre-launch awareness is not current national awareness.; sources: World Bank, 2025: De Jure and De Facto Coverage of Parental Benefits in Nepal https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021925113581657/pdf/P1766171d407e20f21adde1ba735b9a8b83.pdf)
- Aware: 2023: 7 percent of women knew of SSF. (Women informal workers in the same survey; limit: Same pre-launch and urban-sample limits.; sources: World Bank, 2025: De Jure and De Facto Coverage of Parental Benefits in Nepal https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021925113581657/pdf/P1766171d407e20f21adde1ba735b9a8b83.pdf)
- Aware: 2023: 15 percent of men knew of SSF. (Men informal workers in the same survey; limit: Same pre-launch and urban-sample limits.; sources: World Bank, 2025: De Jure and De Facto Coverage of Parental Benefits in Nepal https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021925113581657/pdf/P1766171d407e20f21adde1ba735b9a8b83.pdf)

- Eligible: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Among people who qualify for an allowance, how many hold the documents and have applied?

- Documented: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Among people who qualify for an allowance, how many hold the documents and have applied?

- Applied: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Among people who qualify for an allowance, how many hold the documents and have applied?

- Enrolled: ILO report dated 24 December 2025: about 1500 informal and self-employed registrants. (Informal and self-employed workers; limit: Mixed informal and self-employed categories; no eligible population or benefit-receipt denominator.; sources: International Labour Organization, 2025: Nepal launches national campaign to bring informal workers into social security https://www.ilo.org/resource/news/nepal-launches-national-campaign-bring-informal-workers-social-security)

- Received: 2023 survey: only 6 percent of informal parents received cash benefits at the last birth. (Informal parents in the same survey; limit: Not heat support or current SSF receipt; childbirth may predate the survey.; sources: World Bank, 2025: De Jure and De Facto Coverage of Parental Benefits in Nepal https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021925113581657/pdf/P1766171d407e20f21adde1ba735b9a8b83.pdf)

- Adequate: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Do allowances arrive on time and cover what a hot season costs older people and outdoor-worker households?

- On time: nobody has measured this here yet, in the sources checked. Open question: Do allowances arrive on time and cover what a hot season costs older people and outdoor-worker households?

#### Delivery routes and organisations in Nepal (unranked)

- Ward offices and local governments (government). Receive allowance applications, check documents and maintain registration and transfer processes. Where: Nepal. What it says about itself: No comparable 2026 application-to-receipt count extracted.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Department of National ID and Civil Registration: प्राय सोधिने प्रश्नहरु : सामाजिक सुरक्षा https://www.donidcr.gov.np/pages/mostly-asked-questions--social-security-4/

- Banks participating in social allowance payment (financial). Provide allowance accounts and collection; FAQ describes arrangements for people needing assistance. Where: Nepal. What it says about itself: No measured heat-season collection or delay total extracted.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Department of National ID and Civil Registration: प्राय सोधिने प्रश्नहरु : सामाजिक सुरक्षा https://www.donidcr.gov.np/pages/mostly-asked-questions--social-security-4/

- Health Insurance Board registration assistants (government). Help households enrol through ward-level and household contact routes. Where: Nepal. What it says about itself: No verified assisted-enrolment or heat-claim outcome count extracted.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Health Insurance Board: बारम्बार सोधिने प्रश्नहरू https://hib.gov.np/faq/

- Nepal Red Cross Society (civil society). The heatwave protocol assigns volunteer support and cash-delivery tasks. Where: Four protocol municipalities. What it says about itself: Plan: 1,200 households; not a confirmed receipt count.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/downloadfile/93851/sEAP2025NP02_MDRNP020

- Female Community Health Volunteers (government). The heat protocol includes household contact through frontline volunteers. Where: Protocol locations. What it says about itself: Planned activity only; delivered reach not verified.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/downloadfile/93851/sEAP2025NP02_MDRNP020

- Save the Children (civil society). Publishes a local-government allowance-access guidance catalogue. Where: Nepal. What it says about itself: No independently verified navigation outcome count extracted.. What independent studies found: none found in the sources checked. Sources: Save the Children, 2026: Ensuring access to social security allowances in Nepal: Guidance for local governments on developing and implementing a standard operating procedure https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/ensuring-access-to-social-security-allowances-in-nepal-guidance-for-local-governments-on-developing-and-implementing-a-standard-operating-procedure
